readout_other: Compound action potential (CAP) amplitude and conduction velocity (CV), recorded via bipolar electrodes and a digital oscilloscope
direction_notes: 1 W continuous-wave ultrasound increased both conduction velocity and CAP amplitude, whereas 2 and 3 W increased conduction velocity but progressively decreased CAP amplitude, an effect attributed largely to ultrasonic thermal effects.

exposures.label: Continuous-wave ultrasound (1, 2, or 3 W acoustic power) applied to excised sciatic nerve

timing.protocol_description: The ultrasound stimulation system was switched on to expose the nerve tissue to continuous wave ultrasound radiation at 1, 2, and 3 W. For each measurement, the sciatic nerve was stimulated by ultrasound for 5 min and its CAP signal was collected once per second.

source_quotes.n_subjects: The measurements were performed on five nerve samples for each of the three ultrasound energies used.
